messages:
Ethan: heads up — hit a weird KV cache eviction + memory growth pattern on Qwen-variant when running long-context chat sims (>200k tokens). attaching short repro logs below.

Jules: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro? is this new after the slab coalesce change? :thinking_face: 

Ethan: repro steps in the logs: start with 1 x qwen-13b-mfa, request stream of 220k tokens with mixed user/system prefixes. observed steady growth in RSS and periodic ~10-20% eviction spikes that then 'snap back' and grow again. pid log: `rss: 12.4G -> 13.6G -> 11.1G -> 14.0G` over 45m.

Priya: can you dump KV residency and page map at the spike? `kvctl dump-residency --pid $PID` should show slab occupancy.

Ethan: pasted snippet: ```
# kvctl dump-residency
slab0: used=92% free=8% frag=14% pages=18432
slab1: used=44% free=56% frag=6% pages=8192
page_allocs: 1.2M
recent_evictions: 27
last_eviction_policy: rope-aware
```

Sam: interesting that slab0 is near full but frag=14% not horrendous. what model config? mqa/gqa? rope scaling config?

Ethan: model: qwen-13b-rev, using MQA mode with rope_scaling=auto (we recently enabled fudge factor 1.025). kernel path: `int8-mqa-opt` after kernel selector.

Devon: could be interplay of rope scaling length increase causing more KV rows to be allocated than expected, then coalesce kicks in and compacts, causing the short RSS drop then regrowth. Do we see lots of small allocations (stripes) rather than contiguous pages?

Ethan: yes, /proc/pid/smaps shows many small anonymous mappings during growth window. pmap shows many 4k-backed anonymous pages.

Priya: put a quick patch suggestion: lower the slab coalesce aggressiveness for MQA when rope_scaling != disabled. i.e. change threshold from 64 -> 128 contiguous pages before coalesce to avoid frequent compaction cycles.

Jules: that'd reduce compaction churn but might increase fragmentation. Have we seen fragmentation regressions on Llama/Mistral with that change?

Devon: Llama/Mistral tended to prefer smaller coalesce threshold historically (they allocate larger contiguous KV blocks), Qwen's MQA seems to produce many narrow rows per token. So heuristics should be model-aware.

Sam: can we add a quick telemetry tag for `kv-coalesce-reason` and `kv-alloc-pattern` so we can correlate spikes to kernel selection outcomes? simple counter: ++coalesce_{reason} with labels.

Ethan: done a local run with profiling: attached flame: peak at `page_coalesce` + `kv_sweep` during the snapback. also see `kernel_migration` events when we hit 8192-page boundary.

perf-bot: [auto] recorded profile 3123456789-1, flame id flm-20260318-313. use /perf view flm-20260318-313 for details.

Priya: next steps: (1) reproduce on dedicated Qwen instance with controlled rope scale upping, (2) toggle slab coalesce threshold per-model, (3) add telemetry counters and short-term circuit to prefer non-coalescing fallback when eviction rate > 10/min.

Jules: +1. also add a short experiment: try running with kernel selector forced to `gqa-fallback` and see if allocation pattern changes (we suspect kernel-specific KV layout differences).

Ethan: will run those tonight and post a short summary. thanks all. :pray:

qa-bot: regression test queued: kv-eviction-snapback-qwen -> test 3123456789-qt. I'll run multitenant sim with 3 conc clients.

Sam: if anyone has quick commands for capturing page map diffs, use `for t in 1 2 3; do kvctl snapshot --pid $PID --out /tmp/kvsnap-$t; sleep 30; done` then `kvctl diff /tmp/kvsnap-1 /tmp/kvsnap-3`. saves us from manual smaps parsing.

Ethan: perfect, posting diffs after runs. will also try coalesce threshold toggle (env REDWOOD_KV_COALESCE=128) to test.

Devon: sounds good. if problem reproduces, we should make a rolling canary tweak to threshold for Qwen customers only.

Ethan: noted. will follow up with results tomorrow.
